extracted.intended_audience: Researchers preparing/submitting NIH R01 (Parent R01, NIAID) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: A complete, sample NIH Research Project Grant (R01) application and associated forms illustrating required sections, formats, and content (Project Summary/Abstract, Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Facilities & Other Resources, Biosketches, Human/Animal subject sections, etc.) for investigators applying to NIAID/NIH.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA and application-format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required SF424 (R&R) form fields and submission metadata
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the SF 424 (R&R) Application for Federal Assistance with required submission metadata (type of submission, federal identifier routing numbers, dates submitted, applicant information, authorized representative signature, UEI, applicant address, contact person).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields shown include: Type of Submission; Federal Identifier; Date Submitted; Applicant legal name and address; Person to be contacted on matters involving this application; Authorized Representative name/signature/date; Tracking Number; Funding Opportunity Number; Received Date. Provide accurate contact and institutional UEI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble and include all required application components (Table of Contents)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide all sections listed in the application Table of Contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required components listed: SF 424 R&R Cover Page; Performance Sites; Research & Related Other Project Information; Project Summary/Abstract (Description); Project Narrative; Facilities & Other Resources; Equipment; Research & Related Senior/Key Person; PHS398 Cover Page Supplement; PHS 398 Modular Budget; Personnel Justification; PHS 398 Research Plan (Specific Aims, Research Strategy); PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information; Bibliography & References Cited; Letters of Support; Resource Sharing Plan(s); Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources. Include file names and page numbers for attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Summary/Abstract must summarize objectives, hypothesis, rationale, specific aims, innovation, expected outcomes and significance to public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should state long-term goal, objective of proposal, prior work basis, central hypothesis, specific aims (e.g., Aim 1, Aim 2, Aim 3), rationale, innovation (how the approach differs/novel), and expected outcomes and significance (potential impact on understanding/treatment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative — public health relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Project Narrative that explains why the proposed research is relevant to public health and to NIH's mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how the research will reduce burden of disease or seek fundamental knowledge about living systems. Keep the narrative concise and focused on public health relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — describe scientific environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities, laboratory and office space, equipment, computational resources, core facilities access, and intellectual environment that will support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include square footage, specific rooms (e.g., dark room, microscopy rooms), availability of microscopes, imaging systems, storage (freezers), incubators, shared cores (mass spectrometry, genomics, light microscopy), computational clusters, network-attached storage, and descriptions of collaborative interactions and seminar/meeting opportunities. Mention administrative/logistical support available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment — list major equipment and shared resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specifics on major equipment available to the project and access to shared instrumentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List instrument models and capabilities (e.g., Zeiss LSM700 confocal, ImageXpress Nano, Orbitrap MS, BioRad qPCR, Copas Biosort), and note access to neighboring/shared equipment and core facility instruments and services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard/Biosafety plan and authorizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe biosafety approvals, relevant BUAs, procedures for handling/disposal of pathogens, required PPE and training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include BUA number and IBC approval coverage, specify biosafety level (e.g., Orsay virus is BSL1; lab BUA may cover BSL2 pathogens), and outline training and PPE (gloves, lab coats) and approved procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person profiles and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide expanded profiles for PD/PI and senior/key personnel including project role, credentials, biographical sketch attachments, and current & pending support files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each Senior/Key person include: Name, eRA Commons username, Position Title, Organization, Project Role (e.g., PD/PI), Degree Type and Year, Attach Biographical Sketch (file) and Current & Pending Support (file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch format and content (PHS/NIH) — page limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the required biographical sketch elements and adhere to page limits and formatting instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the PHS-398 biographical sketch format: Name, eRA Commons user name, Position Title, Education/Training (with institution, degree, completion date, field), A. Personal Statement, B. Positions, Scientific Appointments, and Honors, C. Contributions to Science, and Relevant Citations. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether human subjects are involved, specify exemption status, IRB review status, and provide explanations for any use of human specimens/data not considered human subjects research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields include: Are Human Subjects Involved? If YES, Is the Project Exempt? If NO, is IRB review pending or date of IRB approval; provide Human Subject Assurance Number and explanation of non–human-subjects use where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether vertebrate animals are used and provide IACUC review status, approval dates and Animal Welfare Assurance Number where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields include: Are Vertebrate Animals Used? If YES, Is the IACUC review pending? If NO, provide IACUC Approval Date and Animal Welfare Assurance Number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistics, rigor, reproducibility, and sex as a biological variable
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a plan for statistical analysis, experimental replicates, approaches for parametric and non-parametric data, multiple comparisons correction, and considerations of sex as a biological variable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details on technical and biological replicates. For parametric data, state use of Student's t-test (2 groups) or ANOVA (>2 groups) and Tukey's test for post-hoc comparisons after ANOVA (P < 0.05). For non-parametric data, use Mann–Whitney or Kruskal–Wallis ANOVA. Use Benjamini–Hochberg correction to control false discovery rate. State numbers/scale of experiments (e.g., qRT-PCR, RNA-seq, western, metabolomics with thousands of animals; virus quantification with 100+ animals per condition; all assays in at least three independent experiments). Address genetic controls such as using two independently isolated alleles and/or rescue strains to control for mutant background. Declare which sexes/sexes of organisms will be used (e.g., C. elegans hermaphrodites).

rubrics_metrics.name: Power and sample-size considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain rationale for sample sizes and state when power analysis is or is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because number of animals may not be limiting (e.g., with C. elegans), power analysis may not be required for many experiments; nevertheless state typical sample sizes (provided examples: 1000s for some assays, 100+ for virus quantification) and justify replicates and independent experiments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing, data/code management and authentication plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Include plans for resource sharing, authentication of key biological/chemical resources, and code/data management and distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide Resource Sharing Plan(s) and Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources attachments. For software, state repository management (e.g., GitHub) and plan to publicly distribute code upon publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications, assurances and legal attestation
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the authorized representative certifies that statements are true and that the applicant will comply with required assurances; include required certification list or link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Authorized Representative signs to certify statements contained in the list of certifications and required assurances; note warning about false statements and potential penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). Include the list of certifications/assurances or an Internet site where it may be obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA and copyright / permitted reuse notice
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand posting and reuse rules: application text is copyrighted by awardee but NIAID may post application and summary statement for educational purposes, with conditions and FOIA redactions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awardee provided express permission for NIAID to post grant application and summary statement for educational purposes with the condition the material remain unchanged and include credit to PIs, organizations, and NIH NIAID. FOIA responses will be subject to exemptions and include redactions to protect confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments/deliberations, and personal privacy information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 conformance and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure application materials are accessible to people with disabilities and assistive technology users; provide contact for accessibility issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note that the sample was reformatted to improve accessibility; if trouble accessing content contact NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources at deaweb@niaid.nih.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide file attachments and name/mime-types
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach required documents with appropriate filenames and indicate mime types where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in application: Project_Summary.pdf, Project_Narrative.pdf, References.pdf, Facilities_and_Other_Resources_Final.pdf, Equipment.pdf, Cover_Letter.pdf. Include tracking numbers and page references for attachments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose foreign activities and environmental/historic impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether activities occur outside the United States, identify partner countries, and state if project impacts the environment or a historic place and provide explanations if yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fields include: Does this project involve activities outside the United States or partnership with international collaborators? If yes, identify countries. Also indicate if the project has an actual or potential impact on the environment or is designated as a historic place and provide explanations and whether an EA/EIS was performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of appropriate experimental controls and independent validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for controls and independent validation to ensure findings are robust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: perform experiments with two independently isolated alleles and/or rescue strains to control for mutant background; perform assays in multiple independent experiments; include mosaic and transgenic controls when interpreting cell-autonomy and bystander effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific aims and research strategy structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize the research plan into Specific Aims and a Research Strategy that details aims, rationale, methods, expected outcomes, potential pitfalls, and alternative approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample includes three explicit aims with a central hypothesis and rationale, followed by detailed experimental approaches, anticipated outcomes, pitfalls and future directions. Make aims clear, testable, and linked to significance and innovation statements.
